title: His First Day
excerpt: Erotic office romance · Forbidden attraction · Workplace drama
content:
Victoria Hayes believed in three things: punctuality, professionalism, and never mixing business with pleasure.

At thirty-two, she had perfected the art of controlling a room without raising her voice. As the senior executive secretary at Blackwood Enterprises, she managed her director's calendar, prepared confidential documents, and kept an entire department functioning while everyone else took the credit.

Then Daniel Cole arrived.

He was twenty-five, freshly graduated, and irritatingly handsome. His white shirt fitted his shoulders perfectly, his dark hair looked effortlessly messy, and his smile suggested that he knew exactly how attractive he was.

"You're the intern?" Victoria asked, glancing up from her computer.

"Daniel Cole. Reporting for duty."

"You're three minutes late."

"Two minutes and forty seconds, actually."

Victoria slowly raised her eyes.

Daniel's smile widened. "Sorry. First lesson learned."

"Good. Second lesson: don't argue with the woman responsible for your schedule."

"Wouldn't dream of it."

She handed him a folder. Their fingers brushed, and neither moved immediately.

It was barely a second, but Victoria noticed.

She noticed the way he looked at her, too—not rudely, but with an attention that made her suddenly conscious of her fitted blouse and the perfume she had chosen that morning.

"Your desk is beside mine," she said, returning to her screen. "You'll report directly to me for the next three months."

"That sounds promising."

"Your internship, Daniel. I'm talking about your internship."

"Of course, Ms. Hayes."

He said it with such innocent seriousness that she nearly laughed.

By lunchtime, he had already learned how she liked her documents arranged, which executives to avoid before coffee, and exactly how to make her lose her train of thought with an unexpected compliment.

"You always this strict?" he asked while they reviewed a presentation.

"Only when someone needs supervision."

"Then I suppose I'll need a lot of it."

Victoria gave him a warning look. "Concentrate on the slides."

"I am."

"You're looking at me."

"You're standing in front of the screen."

She stepped aside.

He looked at the screen for approximately two seconds before glancing back at her.

"Daniel."

"Victoria."

It was the first time he had used her first name.

Something in the way he said it made the office feel smaller.

She closed the folder. "Let's finish this tomorrow."

"Afraid you'll get distracted?"

"I'm afraid you'll forget you're here to learn."

His expression softened. "I haven't forgotten. But I can learn my job and still think you're beautiful."

Victoria stared at him.

For once, she had no immediate reply.

That evening, most of the office emptied before seven. Victoria remained behind to finish a report, while Daniel worked at the desk beside hers.

Rain tapped against the windows. The city glittered below them.

"You're still here," she observed.

"So are you."

"I'm your supervisor. I have responsibilities."

"And I'm your intern. I have responsibilities too."

She smiled despite herself. "Such as?"

"Making sure you don't work yourself into exhaustion."

He placed a cup of coffee beside her keyboard.

Victoria looked at it, then at him. "You remembered how I take it?"

"Two sugars. No milk."

She hadn't told him.

"How did you know?"

"I pay attention."

That answer stayed between them longer than it should have.

When they finally stood to leave, Daniel reached for the same umbrella she did. Their hands met around its handle.

Neither let go.

"Victoria," he said quietly, "if I'm making you uncomfortable, tell me, and I'll keep things strictly professional."

She studied his face. He wasn't smiling now.

"You should," she whispered.

"Should what?"

"Keep things professional."

He nodded and released the umbrella.

"Goodnight, Ms. Hayes."

He walked away without looking back.

Victoria watched him enter the elevator, annoyed by the strange disappointment settling in her chest.

Her phone buzzed.

A message from Daniel.

One question before I go to sleep.

She should have ignored it.

Instead, she typed: What?

His reply appeared almost immediately.

If I hadn't been assigned to work for you, would you still have told me to keep things professional?

Victoria stared at the screen for a long time.

Then she locked her phone without answering.

But for the first time in months, she went home thinking about someone other than herself.

And she already knew tomorrow would be dangerous.
